cnd12:2.1: Those who answered me before: Bāvarī the brahmin and his other teachers answered, explained, taught, asserted, established, clarified, analyzed, disclosed, and revealed their own view, their own acceptance, their own liking, their own doctrine, their own disposition, and their own intention—
cnd12:2.4: Thus: this is a joining of words … a sequence of words—
cnd12:2.7: Hemaka: this is the name of that brahmin … expression—
cnd12:3.1: Before Gotama’s teaching: before Gotama’s teaching, apart from Gotama’s teaching, previous to Gotama’s teaching, earlier than Gotama’s teaching: the teaching of the Buddha, the teaching of the Victor, the teaching of the Realized One, the teaching of the perfected one—
cnd12:4.1: Thus it was, thus it will be: so they say it was, so they say it will be—
cnd12:5.1: All that was just the testament of hearsay: all that was hearsay, from rumor, from tradition, from the authority of scriptures, through reasoning, through logic, through reflection on appearances, through accepting a view after considering it; they spoke of a teaching that they had not directly known for themselves, that was not witnessed personally—
cnd12:6.1: All that just fostered speculation: all that fostered speculation, fostered thinking, fostered intention, fostered sensual thoughts, fostered malicious thoughts, fostered cruel thoughts, fostered thoughts about relatives, fostered thoughts about the country, fostered thoughts of immortality, fostered thoughts connected with compassion for others, fostered thoughts connected with gain, honor, and fame, and fostered thoughts connected with not being looked down on—
cnd12:7.1: I found no delight in that: I found no delight in that, I did not find it, I did not obtain it, I did not gain it—
cnd12:10.4: Teaching: the spiritual life that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with meaning and with phrasing, entirely full and pure; the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path, and extinguishment and the practice that leads to extinguishment: declare, explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal—
cnd12:11.4: The destruction of craving, the giving up of craving, the stilling of craving, the relinquishment of craving, the allaying of craving: the deathless, extinguishment.
cnd12:11.5: Sage: sagacity is called knowledge … having transcended the net of attachments, they are a sage—
cnd12:12.1: Having understood it, one who lives mindfully: having made it known, weighed it up, judged it, made it clear, and made it evident.
cnd12:12.2: having made known that “all conditions are impermanent”, having weighed it up, judged it, made it clear, and made it evident,
cnd12:12.5: having made known that “anything that has the nature of arising has the nature of ending”, having weighed it up, judged it, made it clear, and made it evident.
cnd12:12.7: developing mindfulness meditation by contemplating the body in the body, they are mindful …
cnd12:12.9: Living: living, dwelling, conducting oneself, carrying on, maintaining oneself, sustaining oneself, and keeping going—
cnd12:13.1: May cross over clinging in the world: clinging is called craving.
cnd12:13.2: That which is desire, strong desire … covetousness, greed, a root of what is unskillful.
cnd12:13.3: Clinging: for what reason is it called clinging? … it is called clinging because it is spread out and extended.
cnd12:13.4: In the world: in the world of the lower realms, the human world, the world of the gods, the world of the aggregates, the world of the elements, the world of the sense fields.
cnd12:13.5: May cross over clinging in the world: this clinging in the world, or that clinging in the world, one who is mindful might cross, cross over, cross beyond, surmount, or transcend—
cnd12:16.4: Sensed: what is smelled with the nose, tasted with the tongue, touched with the body;
cnd12:17.1: Among pleasant things, Hemaka: and what in the world is a pleasant thing, an agreeable thing?
cnd12:17.2: The eye in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing, the ear in the world … the nose in the world … the tongue in the world … the body in the world … the mind in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing;
cnd12:17.3: sights in the world are pleasant and agreeable things, sounds in the world … smells in the world … tastes in the world … touches in the world … ideas in the world are pleasant and agreeable things;
cnd12:17.4: eye consciousness in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing, ear consciousness in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing, nose consciousness in the world … tongue consciousness in the world … body consciousness in the world … mind consciousness in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing, eye contact in the world … ear contact in the world … nose contact in the world … tongue contact in the world … body contact in the world … mind contact in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing;
cnd12:17.5: feeling born of eye contact in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing … feeling born of ear contact … feeling born of nose contact … feeling born of tongue contact … feeling born of body contact … feeling born of mind contact in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing;
cnd12:17.6: perception of sights in the world … perception of sounds in the world … perception of smells in the world … perception of tastes in the world … perception of touches in the world … perception of ideas in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing, intention regarding sights in the world … intention regarding sounds in the world … intention regarding smells in the world … intention regarding tastes in the world … intention regarding touches in the world … intention regarding ideas in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing;
cnd12:17.7: craving for sights in the world … craving for sounds in the world … craving for smells in the world … craving for tastes in the world … craving for touches in the world … craving for ideas in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing;
cnd12:17.8: thought about sights in the world … thought about sounds in the world … thought about smells in the world … thought about tastes in the world … thought about touches in the world … thought about ideas in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing;
cnd12:17.9: consideration of sights in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing, consideration of sounds in the world … consideration of smells in the world … consideration of tastes in the world … consideration of touches in the world … consideration of ideas in the world is a pleasant and agreeable thing—
cnd12:18.2: Desire and lust: that which, regarding sensual pleasures, is sensual desire, sensual lust, relishing of sensual pleasures, craving for sensual pleasures, affection for sensual pleasures, passion for sensual pleasures, infatuation with sensual pleasures, attachment to sensual pleasures, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, grasping at sensual pleasures, the hindrance of sensual desire.
cnd12:18.3: Removal of desire and lust: the giving up of desire and lust, the stilling of desire and lust, the relinquishment of desire and lust, the allaying of desire and lust: the deathless, extinguishment—
cnd12:19.1: The state of extinguishment that does not pass: the state of extinguishment, the state of protection, the state of shelter, the state of refuge, the state of safety.
cnd12:19.2: That does not pass: permanent, stable, eternal, not liable to change—
cnd12:22.3: That which is the stilling of all activities, the relinquishment of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd12:22.4: Having understood: having understood, known, weighed up, judged, made clear, and made evident.
cnd12:22.5: having understood that “all conditions are impermanent”, having known, weighed up, judged, made clear, and made evident.
cnd12:22.8: having understood that “anything that has the nature of arising has the nature of ending”, having known, weighed up, judged, made clear, and made evident.
cnd12:22.11: because they have developed mindfulness meditation by contemplating the body in the body, they are mindful …
cnd12:23.2: Those who have seen the teaching: those who have seen the teaching, known the teaching, weighed up the teaching, judged the teaching, made evident the teaching, and made clear the teaching.
cnd12:23.3: “All conditions are impermanent”: those who have seen the teaching …
cnd12:23.4: “Anything that has the nature of arising has the nature of ending”: those who have seen the teaching, known the teaching, weighed up the teaching, judged the teaching, made evident the teaching, and made clear the teaching.
cnd12:23.5: Quenched: they are quenched because greed has been extinguished, quenched because hate has been extinguished, quenched because delusion has been extinguished, because anger … because acrimony … because all unskillful volitional constructs have been stilled, quieted, calmed, burnt out, quenched, departed, and allayed, they are still, at peace, calmed, quenched, and allayed—
cnd12:24.2: At peace: because greed has been pacified and extinguished they are at peace … because hate … because delusion … because anger … because acrimony … because all unskillful volitional constructs have been stilled, quieted, calmed, burnt out, quenched, departed, and allayed, they are still, at peace, calmed, quenched, and allayed: thus they are at peace.
cnd12:24.4: Always: always, at all times, at every time, at constant times, continually, regularly, without a break, shaft after shaft, like waves rising on water, in unbroken continuity, in close contact, before the meal, after the meal, in the first watch, the middle watch, the last watch, in the dark fortnight, the bright fortnight, in the rains, the winter, the summer, in the early part of life, the middle part of life, the last part of life—
cnd12:25.1: Have crossed over clinging in the world: clinging is called craving.
cnd12:25.2: That which is desire, strong desire … covetousness, greed, a root of what is unskillful.
cnd12:25.3: Clinging: for what reason is it called clinging? … it is called clinging because it is spread out and extended.
cnd12:25.4: In the world: in the world of the lower realms … in the world of the sense fields.
cnd12:25.5: Have crossed over clinging in the world: this clinging in the world, or that clinging in the world, they have crossed, crossed over, crossed out, gone beyond, completely surmounted, and transcended—
cnd12:27.2: The Blessed One is my teacher, sir, and I am a disciple.
